rows.description: I feel treated like a small child and stew in silent anger. Wise: say calmly what the rule costs me and offer a trial of trust. Immature: sulking, slamming doors, or punishing them by dropping my studies.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, contempt, deceit, fear, gratitude, manipulation

rows.description: I start thinking my parents are backward and clueless, so their words stop counting. Wise: separate their fear from their outdated methods and still hear the concern. Immature: sneering and treating them as fools.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, deceit, fear, gratitude, manipulation, protectiveness
related mind states: contempt, fear

rows.description: I am the parent's fear made visible: they picture accidents, bad company, gossip. A teen in this spot should see that rules often come from love plus anxiety, and ask what exactly they fear so it can be addressed.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, contempt, deceit, gratitude, manipulation, protectiveness
related mind states: affection, fear, anxiety

rows.description: I follow a rule I dislike because they have earned my trust before, and I say my disagreement openly. Wise: comply, then negotiate for later. Risk: swallowing every wish just to avoid conflict.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, contempt, deceit, fear, gratitude, manipulation
related mind states: trust

rows.description: I fake tears, praise, or emotional blackmail to get a yes. It works sometimes and leaves me feeling slippery. Wise: notice the habit and make an honest case instead, since trust is what buys freedom.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, contempt, deceit, fear, gratitude, protectiveness
related mind states: trust

rows.description: As the parent I clamp down after seeing my teen change, and I feel shut out. A teen can help by sharing plans and whereabouts freely, which lowers the parent's need to control and grows real autonomy.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, contempt, deceit, gratitude, manipulation, protectiveness
related mind states: anxiety

rows.description: As the teen whose phone is monitored, I feel watched. Wise: ask for a clear reason and a path to more trust, and share enough openly that constant checking is not needed. Harmful: secret accounts.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, contempt, deceit, fear, gratitude, manipulation
related mind states: trust

rows.description: When told to be like the topper cousin, I feel small and defective, as if love depends on marks. Wise: name the hurt to a trusted adult, keep my own goals. Harmful: believing the comparison as truth about my worth.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, envy, indifference, resentment
related mind states: affection, shame, trust, hurt

rows.description: I resent my parent and quietly dislike the cousin who did nothing wrong. Wise: tell the parent how comparison lands and ask for support with my own targets. Immature: sabotaging my work to prove them wrong.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, envy, indifference, shame

rows.description: I am compared aloud at family gatherings and feel judged in front of everyone. It is not my fault, and their pride and anxiety are the source. Wise: ask privately to stop and show effort on my own terms.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, indifference, resentment, shame
